So quick question. Since both node delegation pools and rise staking pools will continuously refill itself using the methods in this chart, is there an additional advtantage to being a node delegator than it is to be a rise staker since delegating nodes is a direct contribution to the game infrustructure?

Node delegation is owning a node license and delegating it to a Pool operator for reward generation to the delegator and the operator.  This is the model for the current File Nodes which distribute the files to players installing the game launcher.  There will be other node types, such as Server Nodes (coming soonish) and Data Nodes (mentioned early on but no updates), and possibly other types.  We don't know how or if the delegation model will apply to these other Node types.  These Nodes, or more specifically the Node Pools, directly contribute to the game infrastructure.

Staking RISE locks the RISE up in a stake pool, effectively reducing the token's float (actively traded supply).  You are rewarded while your tokens are locked up.  This doesn't provide any contribution to the game infrastructure.

These are very different activities.  I hope this helped answer your question. (edited)

When you say risk. Do you mean risk of losing investment or risk of losing gains?

LP risk is called impermanent loss.  This is only realized if you sell your LP position but it can be very real.  This happens when one token in the pair substantially outperforms the other token.  If you were to exit the LP at that time then the tokens you receive back would be worth less than if you had simply held them outside the LP.  The bet is that your LP rewards outperform any impermanent loss you might take. (edited)
Monday, April 6, 2026 at 8:00 PM
So even if theoretically the bottom is in for bitcoin and thr bull market begins, if rise token explodes and cardano goes up slower, I could lose a portion of my initial investment?

Not exactly.  You would still gain, but not gain as much from the tokens if you didn't enter the LP.  You then add any LP rewards you gained in the time period to calculate your overall profit, which could be less than if you didn't enter the LP.  The the impermanent loss isn't realized unless/until you exit the position. (edited)
Monday, April 6, 2026 at 8:29 PM

I suppose you could also look at it as a way to DCA out of your position into the other token while gaining rewards. Contrast this against holding and selling higher.  The difference between those outcomes is the impermanent loss.
